要点：

  • 问题非常工程：3D 资产库里「能收集」不等于「能复用」——它在场景拼装、编辑、渲染、游戏生产与训练数据构建里都可能翻车
  • 失效模式具体：一张好看的 RGB 渲染可以掩盖断开/悬浮的几何、混乱的 UV 组织、以及导入后无法正确解析的材质
  • 作者提出 Diagnostic Rendered Evidence（DRE）：把 beauty、wireframe、UV 缝 + wireframe 三种视图对齐，交给按检查项专用的冻结 ViT 分类器打分，再做后期融合

为什么值得看：AI 批量生成/爬取资产的最大成本是「人肉筛」。把可用性拆成可视证据 + 专用分类器，意味着资产入库前就能自动拦掉断几何、坏 UV 与坏材质——这正是资产管线最该自动化的一段。

中文摘要：大型 3D 资产库让「收集」变容易，却让「能否可靠复用」变难：同一个资产要在场景拼装、编辑、渲染、游戏生产与训练数据构建中都成立。问题在于一张看起来合理的 RGB 渲染图，完全可能掩盖断开的几何、混乱的 UV 组织，或导入后解析失败的材质。作者提出 Diagnostic Rendered Evidence（DRE）：把「美观渲染」「线框」「UV 缝叠加线框」三种视图对齐起来，分别交给按检查项冻结的 ViT 分类器打分，再做后期融合得到可用性判断。对依赖批量生成或抓取资产的管线，这等于在入库前加了一道自动分诊。

主题：AI Native Engine

来源：arXiv·cs.CV（English）

原文发布：2026-11-03

本期推送：2026-11-05

Is This 3D Asset Usable? Beyond the Beauty Render for Asset Curation

Abstract

Large 3D repositories make it easy to collect assets, but difficult to determine whether they can be reused reliably across scene assembly, editing, rendering, game production, and training-data construction. An asset can look plausible in RGB while hiding disconnected geometry, problematic UV organization, or materials that fail to resolve correctly after import. We introduce Diagnostic Rendered Evidence (DRE): aligned beauty, wireframe, and UV-seam-plus-wireframe views scored by pass-specific frozen ViT classifiers and combined through late fusion. On 1,234 human labeled TexVerse assets, nested grouped evaluation achieves 86.36% balanced accuracy and 88.32% bad-asset recall. On a separate, balanced 764 external reference test, DRE achieved 88.9% balanced reference-label accuracy. Our method requires only an imported asset and renderer-derived evidence, without repository identity, creator, popularity, text, or source metadata at inference. Our results support cross-corpus portability and show that purpose built diagnostic views expose defects that just the beauty views can miss. Webpage: https://rbz-99.github.io/is-this-3d-asset-usable/

1 Introduction

Consider a common workflow where we download a model from a large 3D repository. It can look perfectly fine and still be difficult to use. A few RGB views look convincing: the shape is recognizable, the texture appears detailed, and nothing is obviously broken. Yet once the asset enters a 3D workflow, different problems can emerge. The mesh may contain disconnected or irregular geometry, the UV layout may complicate texturing, or materials may fail to resolve correctly after import. None of these problems necessarily prevents the asset from producing an attractive preview.

Repository assets are increasingly reused as structured 3D objects: retrieved and arranged into scenes [25, 1, 17], edited [11], rigged for animation [15], or used in modern image-to-3D pipelines that explicitly represent geometry, UVs, textures, and PBR attributes [3, 19, 23]. Across these uses, plausible RGB appearance does not guarantee reliable reuse.

Large repositories such as ShapeNet [4], Objaverse and Objaverse-XL [8, 7], and TexVerse [26] make this a repository-scale curation problem: How can we determine whether a 3D asset is fit for reuse before selecting it from a large repository?

This requires expert review, that considers appearance, geometry, UV structure, and material behavior. We therefore construct a 1,234-asset TexVerse set annotated by 3D researchers and introduce diagnostic rendered evidence: aligned beauty, wireframe, and UV-seam-plus-wireframe views that expose complementary properties of the same asset. Separate models score each evidence type before late fusion produces the final keep/reject decision. Our scope is operational fitness for reusable textured/PBR assets rather than universal aesthetic quality or asset provenance. On our human-labeled assets, our method reaches 86.36% balanced accuracy and 88.32% bad-asset recall. Controlled ablations show that the structural diagnostic passes provide information beyond a matched beauty-only representation. Our contributions are: 1: We introduce diagnostic rendered evidence for 3D asset curation using aligned beauty, wireframe, and UV-seam-plus-wireframe views. 2: We develop a robust rendering pipeline for heterogeneous repository assets, including guarded material fallbacks and explicit material-resolution provenance. 3: We provide a 1,234-asset expert-annotated benchmark for reusable textured/PBR assets, with a keep/reject rubric covering geometry, UV, material, render, and composition failures.

2 Related Work and Scope

3D assets as reusable components: Recent systems increasingly treat existing 3D assets as reusable components. Holodeck retrieves and arranges Objaverse assets for scene generation [25]; Open-Universe similarly retrieves meshes from uncurated databases and optimizes their placement [1]; and Lay-A-Scene studies object arrangement [17]. Existing assets are also edited [11] and automatically rigged for animation [15]. These settings motivate evaluating asset properties that are not fully captured by a beauty render.

3D curation and quality assessment: Objaverse++ and MeshFleet use filtering and human review to construct higher-quality 3D corpora [14, 2], while generative-3D benchmarks evaluate geometry, texture, and cross-view consistency [13, 20, 27, 10]. Perceptual mesh-quality studies likewise show that geometry and texture jointly affect human judgments [12, 16]. Full-reference metrics assume a known reference [16, 24]; repository curation instead requires judging a single asset without one.

Structured evidence for asset quality: Modern 3D systems explicitly represent geometry, UVs, and materials. Hunyuan3D separates mesh and texture generation [28], SF3D predicts UV-unwrapped geometry and material properties [3], and AssetGen reconstructs geometry and PBR appearance [19]. Related work further models UV and material structure explicitly [5, 22, 23], while UV-specific methods motivate interpreting parameterization in surface context [21, 18]. Our method uses rendered views of these structures as no-reference evidence for asset curation.

3 Methodology

Evidence Generation and Provenance: For each imported GLB, we render synchronized diagnostic passes using fixed camera poses, lighting, background, and framing. Four aligned views are generated per pass and scored independently before late fusion. The beauty pass captures overall appearance and visible rendering or material failures, but may hide structural defects through texture, shading, and lighting. The wireframe pass exposes mesh structure, including disconnected components, irregular triangulation, excessive density, and geometric clutter. These patterns are treated as evidence rather than fixed quality rules. The UV-seam-plus-wireframe pass overlays UV boundaries on the mesh, allowing seam organization to be interpreted in its 3D surface context rather than from a flattened atlas alone.

Repository-Agnostic Evidence: DRE is designed around information that can be obtained from an imported asset rather than from a particular repository. The renderer uses no asset ID, creator, source label, caption, popularity statistic, or repository-specific metadata. It first resolves standard Principled-BSDF base-color inputs, then follows supported graph-connected image textures and guarded fallbacks; when resolution is not possible, it records an explicit unresolved-material state rather than inventing a material interpretation. We also generated 2D UV-island layouts and measurements such as coverage, angular distortion, and texel density. These signals were reviewed by 3D experts and evaluated in additional classifier configurations, but provided little improvement over the surface-aligned diagnostic views. We therefore retain them for review and audit rather than classifier input, particularly since UV packing conventions vary across asset categories and authoring workflows. Figure 1 illustrates the synchronized evidence available to both the reviewer and the classifier. No individual diagnostic pass is treated as ground truth. Human review separates several kinds of concern: low overall curation value, geometry integrity or clutter, UV organization, material-resolution anomalies, missing evidence, and other import or composition problems.

Multi-view Scoring and Fusion: For pass m and view v, a frozen ImageNet ViT-B/16 encoder [9] produces z_m,v∈ℝ⁷⁶⁸. We summarize the four aligned views with their feature-wise mean and standard deviation. A standardized, class-balanced logistic-regression model is then trained separately for beauty, wireframe, and UV-seam-plus-wireframe evidence. Each model produces a probability pₘ(good) describing how strongly that particular type of evidence supports keeping the asset.

4 Learning and Evaluation

We use TexVerse [26] to create our set under CC BY, CC BY-SA, or CC0 licenses. Our supervised set contains 1,234 assets annotated by expert 3D researchers: 866 good and 368 bad. An additional 6,685 assets based on the deterministic render QA and their metadata are used as less weighted auxiliary training data. We use five-fold nested stratified group cross-validation, grouping by creator or source where available. Inner folds train the pass-specific classifiers, generate out-of-fold predictions for fusion, and select weak-label weights, regularization, pass combinations, and the decision threshold. Auxiliary samples sharing a group with the held-out fold are excluded. Metadata and strict full-PBR inventory provide weak-label sources, while terms such as Rodin, photogrammetry, or scan identify low-weight negative candidates rather than evaluation labels. Face count, texture resolution, creator, and source are retained only for audit and stratification. Table 1 reports outer-fold predictions.

Modality Ablation: Table 1 keeps the labels, grouped folds, ViT representation, classifier family, fusion method, and threshold-selection protocol fixed while changing only the render evidence. UV-seam-wire achieves the highest balanced accuracy, while the full three-pass model gives the highest bad recall and fewest false accepts. Thus, the benefit is not simply due to using more views: the structural passes provide information complementary to beauty renders. We exclude material-only views because their appearance is difficult to separate from renderer behavior. A gray render, for example, may indicate an intentional material, scalar input, vertex color, missing texture, or failed graph resolution. Material behavior is therefore audited separately rather than used as a learned visual modality.

Baselines: The matched beauty-only ViT in Table 1 is our primary representation baseline. It keeps the labels, groups, backbone, classifier, fusion, and threshold-selection protocol fixed, isolating the contribution of diagnostic evidence. We also evaluate the released Objaverse++ [14] on our dataset using its 40-view protocol. Our method uses no popularity, creator, source, or text features at inference and requires 12 diagnostic images per asset, compared with 40 RGB views for Objaverse++. Objaverse++ outputs are mapped as High/Superior = keep and Low/Medium = reject.

Our method retains 731 of 866 good assets and admits 43 of 368 bad assets. Objaverse++ retains 245 good assets and admits 62 bad assets. A paired exact McNemar test gives p=1.31×10⁻¹⁰², with 568 assets correct only for our method and 63 correct only for Objaverse++. Further we additionally evaluate cross-corpus portability on a fixed, balanced external reference set of 382 good and 382 bad assets from strict-PBR ABO [6] and Objaverse assets. DRE achieves 88.9% balanced reference-label accuracy, with 80.4% good-reference recall and 97.4% bad-reference recall. Objaverse got about 47.0% balanced reference-label accuracy: although it retains 88.7% of the strict-PBR reference assets, it rejects only 5.2% of the bad assets, admitting 94.8% as good.

Figure 2 shows how diagnostic passes make different failure modes inspectable. Some failures are visible in conventional appearance renders, while others become clear only when the same camera poses expose geometry or UV seams. The diagnostic representation does not turn mesh density or seam count into hard rules. It gives reviewers and the classifier evidence that can be interpreted in the context of the asset and its intended downstream use.

5 Conclusion

A beauty render can indicate whether an asset looks plausible, but not whether it is operationally fit for reliable reuse. Diagnostic evidence for appearance, topology, UV structure, and material resolution makes the relevant conditions inspectable from the asset itself. By separating these evidence types before fusion, DRE provides a repository-agnostic basis for quality-controlled asset selection for various workflows.

（参考文献见原文。）

item.title: 生成、编辑、补全其实是同一件事：SeMo3D 只重画「指定区域」，其余保持不动 ｜ SeMo3D: Unifying 3D Generation, Editing, and Completion via Selective Modeling
item.description:
一句话：三个任务都在「合成指定区域、保留其余部分」；按任务分别重生成会带来不一致与配对数据依赖。

要点：

  • 现状问题：3D 生成、编辑与补全通常各自被当作「在任务特定约束下重新生成整个资产」，即使只需要改一小块
  • 代价有三条：任务之间彼此隔离、本该不变的内容出现不一致、并且依赖任务专用的成对数据
  • SeMo3D 的关键观察是三者本质相同——都是「合成指定区域、保持其余部分完整」（生成时指定区域就是全区域），因此可以统一建模

为什么值得看：资产迭代的真实形态是「改一处」，而不是「重生成一遍」。把三种任务统一成「选择性建模」，直接对应美术的局部修改工作流，也顺带减少对成对训练数据的依赖。

中文摘要：3D 生成、编辑与补全通常被当作三个独立任务，各自在任务特定约束下重新生成整个资产——哪怕只需要改动一小块区域。这带来三个代价：任务彼此隔离、本该保持不变的内容出现不一致、以及依赖任务专用的成对数据。SeMo3D 从一个简单观察出发：三件事本质上是同一件事——合成指定区域、同时保持其余部分完整（生成时「指定区域」就是全部区域）。据此提出选择性建模来统一三者，让局部修改只动该动的地方。对实际资产迭代（改一处、其余不动）来说，这比每次重生成更贴近工作流。

主题：AI Rendering

来源：arXiv·cs.GR（English）

原文发布：2026-11-03

本期推送：2026-11-05

SeMo3D: Unifying 3D Generation, Editing, and Completion
via Selective Modeling

Abstract

3D generation, editing, and completion are typically treated as regenerating the complete 3D asset under task-specific constraints, even when only a local region needs modification. This leads to task isolation, inconsistency in content that should remain unchanged, and dependence on task-specific paired data. We address these issues with a key observation: the three tasks all synthesize a designated region while keeping the rest intact—the full region for generation, the target region for editing, and the missing region for completion. We term this paradigm Selective Modeling and build SeMo3D upon it; it naturally unifies the three tasks, preserves unchanged content by construction, and enables training without paired editing or completion data, since any 3D asset can be partitioned into a selected region and its context. For training, we propose region-selective denoising, which randomly selects regions of varying sizes on standard 3D assets and applies noise and loss only to them, jointly learning all three tasks. For architecture, we propose Omni3DiT, a multi-condition 3D diffusion transformer that distinguishes regions to create from those to retain and fuses image, text, and point guidance for fine-grained control. Experiments across three benchmarks show SeMo3D surpasses state-of-the-art methods on all tasks, delivering multimodal controllability in generation and strong consistency and accuracy in editing and completion. SeMo3D further serves as a unified modeling tool for agents, enabling efficient 3D creation through natural-language interaction. Project page: https://xiaokunsun.github.io/SeMo3D.github.io/.

1 Introduction

3D content creation—spanning generation [36, 40], editing [21], completion [84], and their combinations—is central to games [92], AR/VR [44, 1], robotics [12, 55], and digital twins [47]. Although typically studied in isolation, these tasks are conventionally viewed through the same lens: regenerating a complete 3D asset under task-specific constraints—matching the condition for generation, and additionally the source asset for editing or the partial input for completion. A unified framework covering all three within one model is thus appealing yet remains an open problem.

Driven by generative models [23, 41] and large-scale 3D datasets [14, 13], all three tasks have advanced rapidly. As illustrated in Fig.2(a), mainstream feed-forward approaches [78, 77, 76, 72, 11, 56] share a common paradigm we term holistic modeling: creating the complete 3D asset under image or text guidance. To preserve consistency with the source, editing and completion methods [76, 72, 11, 56] additionally condition on the source asset or partial input, yet they still regenerate the entire object even when only a local region needs to be modified.111 In this paper, editing refers to local operations like addition, deletion, or replacement, not global operations like style transfer. This creates a fundamental mismatch between what needs to change and what is actually modeled, which leads to three key limitations. (1) Task isolation. As each task imposes a different constraint, generation [78, 94, 77], editing [76, 46, 72], and completion [45, 11, 25] rely on separate models with distinct architectures and objectives, duplicating design and training effort across tasks and multiplying deployment costs. (2) Region inconsistency. Because the full asset is regenerated, source fidelity can only be encouraged rather than guaranteed, and regions that should remain intact are frequently altered (black boxes in Fig.2(a)). (3) Editing/completion data dependency. Regenerating a whole asset that respects the source demands source–target supervision, so many editing [76, 93, 72, 19] and completion [45, 11, 25] methods require costly large-scale paired datasets (e.g., PartFlow [72] curates 100K editing pairs via a seven-stage pipeline), limiting scalability. Moreover, most methods accept only a single guidance modality (image or text), offering limited control: text lacks geometric precision, while images leave occluded regions ambiguous.

Our key observation is that, despite their different constraints, the three tasks share a common structure: synthesizing a designated region while keeping the rest intact—the full, target, and missing regions for generation, editing, and completion. This motivates selective modeling: given an asset represented by spatially aligned tokens (e.g., structured latents [78, 77]), the model synthesizes only the selected tokens and reuses the rest (Fig.2(b)), unlike holistic modeling. Selective modeling thus (1) unifies the three tasks, which differ only in the selected region; (2) preserves unchanged content by construction, as context tokens are never regenerated;222 In this paper, preservation “by construction” holds at the token level: context tokens stay exactly unchanged. Given the near-lossless reconstruction of structured latents [77], this virtually equals asset-level preservation. and (3) requires no task-specific paired data, since any ordinary asset can be partitioned into a selected region and its context. This resolves the three limitations above in a single paradigm.

Based on this insight, we present SeMo3D, a multi-condition model unifying 3D generation, editing, and completion via Selective Modeling, as illustrated in Fig.1. We instantiate selective modeling through two key components. On the training side, we propose region-selective denoising: randomly selecting regions of varying sizes on ordinary 3D assets, adding noise only to the selected tokens, and denoising them while keeping the rest clean. As the selected region ranges from a small portion to the full region, this single procedure spans the entire task spectrum, from local editing through partial completion to full generation, without task-specific paired supervision. On the architecture side, we design Omni3DiT, a unified multi-condition 3D diffusion transformer that jointly processes clean context and noisy selected tokens, and further fuses complementary image, text, and point conditions for fine-grained control. Experiments on three benchmarks show that SeMo3D outperforms specialized state-of-the-art methods on all tasks, with flexible multi-condition control in generation and high-fidelity preservation in editing and completion. SeMo3D further supports agentic and interactive 3D modeling through natural-language interaction.

Our contributions are summarized as follows:

  • •

    We formulate selective modeling, a unified paradigm that casts 3D generation, editing, and completion as synthesizing the designated region while preserving the rest, and present SeMo3D to instantiate this paradigm.

  • •

    We introduce region-selective denoising, which learns all three tasks from standard 3D datasets alone, without costly large-scale paired editing or completion datasets.

  • •

    We develop Omni3DiT, a multi-condition 3D diffusion transformer integrating clean 3D context with image, text, and point guidance for unified controllable 3D creation.

    • 2 Related Work

    3D Generation. Driven by 2D generative models [23, 62, 61, 41, 54, 50], 3D generation has undergone rapid paradigm shifts. Early methods [51, 59, 68, 8, 52] use score distillation sampling (SDS) to lift 2D priors to 3D, but suffer from long optimization times. Multi-view 2D methods [42, 43, 73, 67, 79] accelerate generation by first synthesizing multi-view images and then producing 3D shapes in a feed-forward manner. More recently, native 3D generative models [94, 95, 78, 77, 97, 28, 87, 74, 20, 32] operating directly on 3D latents have pushed quality and scalability further. Despite this progress, most methods condition on a single modality (image or text), limiting fine-grained controllability. Recent efforts incorporate pairwise combinations such as image-text [7, 9] or image-point [75, 29], but none of the above jointly leverages all three modalities to combine the visual detail of images, the semantic expressiveness of text, and the geometric precision of points.

    3D Editing and Completion. 3D editing and completion have evolved analogously: from SDS-based optimization [57, 101, 38, 10, 100, 30, 27] through multi-view 2D methods [4, 35, 3, 18, 16, 70] to native 3D approaches [76, 72, 25, 45, 56, 11]. Native 3D methods are training-free or training-based. Training-free methods [34, 91, 99, 26, 31, 82] repurpose pretrained generators via inversion or optimization; they largely maintain source consistency but require slow, multi-step pipelines. Training-based methods [76, 46, 72, 6, 80, 19, 93, 71, 45, 11, 56, 15, 25] enable fast feed-forward inference but rely on large paired editing or completion datasets (e.g., 100K pairs in PartFlow [72], 116K in 3DEditFormer [76]) and often alter regions that should remain unchanged. Moreover, both lines mostly use a single modality, limiting controllability.

    Unified 3D Multimodal Models. Recent works [90, 88, 85, 86, 89] consolidate multimodal output capabilities into one model, typically unifying 3D understanding with generation and editing [90, 88, 85, 89] or bridging 2D and 3D generation [86]. However, these models are largely built on VLM-based architectures, limiting their native 3D modeling capacity, and their notion of “unity” centers on merging different output modalities (e.g., text, image, and 3D) rather than different 3D creation sub-tasks (generation, editing, and completion). They also typically condition on only one or two modalities, and those that support editing still rely on large-scale paired editing supervision.

    Compared with all three lines of work above, SeMo3D offers a distinct solution: it recasts 3D generation, editing, and completion as a single selective-modeling problem formulated directly on native 3D representations, unifying the three tasks without task-specific architectures or per-task paired supervision while preserving the remaining content by construction. Additionally, SeMo3D supports joint image, text, and point conditioning, enhancing controllability.

    3 Methodology

    3.1 Preliminaries

    Structured Latents. Following Trellis2 [77], we represent 3D assets as spatially structured latent tokens through a three-stage encoding. The first stage, sparse structure (SS), encodes a 3D asset into a dense latent grid Zˢˢ∈ℝ^N³×dₛ covering all N³ voxels, from which an SS decoder recovers the occupied voxel set O. The second and third stages, collectively termed structured latent (SLat) stages, produce sparse tokens only at positions in O: shape tokens Zˢʰᵃᵖᵉ∈ℝ^|O|×d_g encoding fine geometry, and texture tokens Zᵗᵉˣ∈ℝ^|O|×dₜ encoding PBR materials conditioned on Zˢʰᵃᵖᵉ. Each token at every stage corresponds to a localized spatial region, making the representation amenable to spatially selective operations.

    Rectified Flow Matching. Each stage employs a rectified flow model [41, 39] to generate its respective latent tokens. Given data x₀ and noise ε ∼ ℕ(0,I), the forward process linearly interpolates between them as xₜ=(1-t) x₀+t ε for t ∈ [0,1]. A velocity network v_θ is trained by minimizing the conditional flow matching (CFM) objective:

    L_CFM=𝔼_t, x₀, ε\lVertv_θ(xₜ,t,c)-(ε-x₀)\rVert₂²,

    		(1)

    where c denotes the input conditions, and samples are drawn by integrating the learned ODE from t=1 (pure noise) to t=0 (data). All three stages share this formulation; they differ only in x₀ (Zˢˢ, Zˢʰᵃᵖᵉ, or Zᵗᵉˣ, respectively) and in the model that operates on each.

    3.2 Overview

    Fig.3 illustrates the overall framework. For a given stage, let Z={zᵢ}_i∈I denote its structured latent tokens, where I indexes all token positions (all N³ voxels for SS; the occupied set O for SLat). We partition I into a selected setS (to be synthesized) and a context setℂ (to be preserved), where S∪ℂ=I and S∩ℂ=∅. The model denoises only the tokens in S while keeping tokens in ℂ clean. The three tasks differ solely in how this partition is defined: generation selects the full region (S=I, ℂ=∅); editing, the target region; and completion, the missing region.

    SeMo3D instantiates this paradigm at each of the three stages, with a dedicated flow model per stage. For training, region-selective denoising (Sec.3.3, Fig.3(a)) randomly partitions tokens of ordinary 3D assets and applies noise and loss only to S, so one procedure spans all three tasks without per-task paired supervision. For the architecture, Omni3DiT (Sec.3.4, Fig.3(b)) jointly processes clean context tokens and noisy selected tokens, fusing image, text, and point guidance for controllable synthesis. At inference, image guidance is required; text and sparse points are independently optional.

    3.3 Region-Selective Denoising

    As shown in Fig.3(a), unlike the standard objective (Eq.1) that treats all tokens uniformly, region-selective denoising applies noise and loss only to the selected set S while keeping context tokens in ℂ intact. We describe the training and inference procedures below.

    Training. Given the tokens Z of an ordinary 3D asset and a partition (S,ℂ), we construct a mixed input z̃ₜ by adding noise only to tokens in S while keeping tokens in ℂ clean:

    z̃_t,i=\begincases(1-t) z_0,i+t εᵢ,&i∈S, z_0,i,&i∈ℂ,\endcases

    		(2)

    where z_0,i is the clean token at position i. The model takes z̃ₜ together with a binary mask distinguishing S from ℂ, and predicts the velocity field over all positions. The loss is computed only over S; predictions on ℂ are discarded:

    L_RSD=𝔼_t, z₀, ε, S (1)/(|S|)∑_i∈S\lVertv_θ(z̃ₜ,t,c)ᵢ-(εᵢ-z_0,i)\rVert₂².

    		(3)

    Here, 1/|S| normalizes the loss across selected-set sizes. Each step samples one of two partition modes with equal probability: (1) full-region mode (generation) selects all positions (S=I, ℂ=∅), reducing Eq.3 to the CFM objective (Eq.1) scaled by 1/|I|; (2) local-region mode (editing/completion) selects tokens within a random 3D box.

    Inference. Tokens in S start from pure noise and are denoised via ODE integration; tokens in ℂ stay clean. The partition is task-dependent: for generation, the full region is selected (S=I); for editing, the user provides a mask of the target region; for completion, the missing region is either user-specified or derived as the complement of the partial input’s occupancy; as the SS stage decides occupancy within S, only the actually missing geometry is synthesized. The three stages run sequentially: the SS stage denoises S to produce O; the SLat stages inherit the same partition, restricted to O, for shape and texture synthesis.

    Benefiting from training regions ranging from a small portion to the full region, the model covers local editing, partial completion, and full generation in one framework, and, though trained only with boxes, handles free-form target and missing regions (Sec.4.2). Tokens in ℂ are never regenerated, guaranteeing source consistency by construction. Moreover, all three tasks are learned from standard 3D assets without costly per-task paired supervision.

    3.4 Omni3DiT

    Omni3DiT extends Trellis2’s three-stage image-conditioned 3D DiT [50] with four key designs to enable selective modeling with optional text and point guidance (Fig.3(b)): role embedding, text conditioning, point conditioning, and compositional condition dropout.

    Role Embedding. In selective modeling, z̃ₜ (Eq.2) mixes tokens at different noise levels: tokens in S carry noise at timestep t, while tokens in ℂ remain clean.     Text Conditioning. Trellis2 conditions only on images via DINOv3 [60] cross-attention, yet images cannot describe occluded content. We add a parallel cross-attention text branch [9, 7] injecting CLIP [53] features. Both branches share one query and sum their outputs into a residual stream. The text branch output projection is zero-initialized, leaving the pretrained pathway initially undisturbed.

    Point Conditioning. Image and text provide rich visual and semantic guidance but cannot specify exact 3D locations. We therefore add points as a third condition, using sparse rather than dense points since they make user interaction far easier. In the SS stage, each point is represented by a shared learnable embedding, positioned via RoPE [64] at its voxel coordinate, and concatenated into the token sequence [33].     Compositional Condition Dropout. Naively finetuning with all conditions active risks letting the pretrained image branch dominate, suppressing the newly added text and point pathways. At each training step, a random subset of modalities is kept active while the rest are replaced with null embeddings. The probabilities are set so that the image condition is frequently withheld, compelling the text and point branches to independently carry the full guidance load.

    4 Experiments

    Built on these components, SeMo3D supports agentic 3D creation through successive natural-language instructions when integrated with an agent (Fig.4). We report key settings and results here; further details are in the Supp. Mat.

    Implementation Details. We reuse Trellis2’s pretrained SC-VAE [77] and finetune its three-stage flow models at 512 resolution on Trellis-500K [78] with learning rate 5×10⁻⁵ and batch size 32. Fig.5 shows why: for the cake (row 1), text-only Trellis produces the tiers and candles but misses the reference appearance; image-only methods match the appearance but miss the tiers hidden from view, while SeMo3D recovers the hidden tiers with points fixing the layout. Images thus specify appearance, text semantics, and points spatial layout, together producing more faithful results than any single modality.

    3D Editing.Fig.6 and Tab.2 show editing comparisons on Edit3D-Bench. SeMo3D leads across all three metric groups. SeMo3D achieves these results without paired editing data, learning editing entirely from ordinary 3D assets—a practical advantage over data-hungry methods like 3DEditFormer [76] and PartFlow [72].

    3D Completion.Fig.7 and Tab.3 report completion results on Omni-Comp. SeMo3D achieves the best CD, EMD, and F-Score. Even without additional point guidance, SeMo3D outperforms all compared methods across all three completion metrics. Unlike point-guided HY3D-Omni, which regenerates whole shapes, SeMo3D preserves existing geometry, synthesizing only the missing part, despite its irregular, non-box shape. In Fig.7, completed regions blend seamlessly with the existing structure. No paired completion data is used; SeMo3D derives this capability purely from region-selective denoising on standard 3D assets, demonstrating the generality of selective modeling.

一句话：三个任务都在「合成指定区域、保留其余部分」；按任务分别重生成会带来不一致与配对数据依赖。

要点：

  • 现状问题：3D 生成、编辑与补全通常各自被当作「在任务特定约束下重新生成整个资产」，即使只需要改一小块
  • 代价有三条：任务之间彼此隔离、本该不变的内容出现不一致、并且依赖任务专用的成对数据
  • SeMo3D 的关键观察是三者本质相同——都是「合成指定区域、保持其余部分完整」（生成时指定区域就是全区域），因此可以统一建模

为什么值得看：资产迭代的真实形态是「改一处」，而不是「重生成一遍」。把三种任务统一成「选择性建模」，直接对应美术的局部修改工作流，也顺带减少对成对训练数据的依赖。

中文摘要：3D 生成、编辑与补全通常被当作三个独立任务，各自在任务特定约束下重新生成整个资产——哪怕只需要改动一小块区域。这带来三个代价：任务彼此隔离、本该保持不变的内容出现不一致、以及依赖任务专用的成对数据。SeMo3D 从一个简单观察出发：三件事本质上是同一件事——合成指定区域、同时保持其余部分完整（生成时「指定区域」就是全部区域）。据此提出选择性建模来统一三者，让局部修改只动该动的地方。对实际资产迭代（改一处、其余不动）来说，这比每次重生成更贴近工作流。

主题：AI Rendering

来源：arXiv·cs.GR（English）

原文发布：2026-11-03

本期推送：2026-11-05

SeMo3D: Unifying 3D Generation, Editing, and Completion
via Selective Modeling

Abstract

3D generation, editing, and completion are typically treated as regenerating the complete 3D asset under task-specific constraints, even when only a local region needs modification. This leads to task isolation, inconsistency in content that should remain unchanged, and dependence on task-specific paired data. We address these issues with a key observation: the three tasks all synthesize a designated region while keeping the rest intact—the full region for generation, the target region for editing, and the missing region for completion. We term this paradigm Selective Modeling and build SeMo3D upon it; it naturally unifies the three tasks, preserves unchanged content by construction, and enables training without paired editing or completion data, since any 3D asset can be partitioned into a selected region and its context. For training, we propose region-selective denoising, which randomly selects regions of varying sizes on standard 3D assets and applies noise and loss only to them, jointly learning all three tasks. For architecture, we propose Omni3DiT, a multi-condition 3D diffusion transformer that distinguishes regions to create from those to retain and fuses image, text, and point guidance for fine-grained control. Experiments across three benchmarks show SeMo3D surpasses state-of-the-art methods on all tasks, delivering multimodal controllability in generation and strong consistency and accuracy in editing and completion. SeMo3D further serves as a unified modeling tool for agents, enabling efficient 3D creation through natural-language interaction. Project page: https://xiaokunsun.github.io/SeMo3D.github.io/.

1 Introduction

3D content creation—spanning generation [36, 40], editing [21], completion [84], and their combinations—is central to games [92], AR/VR [44, 1], robotics [12, 55], and digital twins [47]. Although typically studied in isolation, these tasks are conventionally viewed through the same lens: regenerating a complete 3D asset under task-specific constraints—matching the condition for generation, and additionally the source asset for editing or the partial input for completion. A unified framework covering all three within one model is thus appealing yet remains an open problem.

Driven by generative models [23, 41] and large-scale 3D datasets [14, 13], all three tasks have advanced rapidly. As illustrated in Fig.2(a), mainstream feed-forward approaches [78, 77, 76, 72, 11, 56] share a common paradigm we term holistic modeling: creating the complete 3D asset under image or text guidance. To preserve consistency with the source, editing and completion methods [76, 72, 11, 56] additionally condition on the source asset or partial input, yet they still regenerate the entire object even when only a local region needs to be modified.111 In this paper, editing refers to local operations like addition, deletion, or replacement, not global operations like style transfer. This creates a fundamental mismatch between what needs to change and what is actually modeled, which leads to three key limitations. (1) Task isolation. As each task imposes a different constraint, generation [78, 94, 77], editing [76, 46, 72], and completion [45, 11, 25] rely on separate models with distinct architectures and objectives, duplicating design and training effort across tasks and multiplying deployment costs. (2) Region inconsistency. Because the full asset is regenerated, source fidelity can only be encouraged rather than guaranteed, and regions that should remain intact are frequently altered (black boxes in Fig.2(a)). (3) Editing/completion data dependency. Regenerating a whole asset that respects the source demands source–target supervision, so many editing [76, 93, 72, 19] and completion [45, 11, 25] methods require costly large-scale paired datasets (e.g., PartFlow [72] curates 100K editing pairs via a seven-stage pipeline), limiting scalability. Moreover, most methods accept only a single guidance modality (image or text), offering limited control: text lacks geometric precision, while images leave occluded regions ambiguous.

Our key observation is that, despite their different constraints, the three tasks share a common structure: synthesizing a designated region while keeping the rest intact—the full, target, and missing regions for generation, editing, and completion. This motivates selective modeling: given an asset represented by spatially aligned tokens (e.g., structured latents [78, 77]), the model synthesizes only the selected tokens and reuses the rest (Fig.2(b)), unlike holistic modeling. Selective modeling thus (1) unifies the three tasks, which differ only in the selected region; (2) preserves unchanged content by construction, as context tokens are never regenerated;222 In this paper, preservation “by construction” holds at the token level: context tokens stay exactly unchanged. Given the near-lossless reconstruction of structured latents [77], this virtually equals asset-level preservation. and (3) requires no task-specific paired data, since any ordinary asset can be partitioned into a selected region and its context. This resolves the three limitations above in a single paradigm.

Based on this insight, we present SeMo3D, a multi-condition model unifying 3D generation, editing, and completion via Selective Modeling, as illustrated in Fig.1. We instantiate selective modeling through two key components. On the training side, we propose region-selective denoising: randomly selecting regions of varying sizes on ordinary 3D assets, adding noise only to the selected tokens, and denoising them while keeping the rest clean. As the selected region ranges from a small portion to the full region, this single procedure spans the entire task spectrum, from local editing through partial completion to full generation, without task-specific paired supervision. On the architecture side, we design Omni3DiT, a unified multi-condition 3D diffusion transformer that jointly processes clean context and noisy selected tokens, and further fuses complementary image, text, and point conditions for fine-grained control. Experiments on three benchmarks show that SeMo3D outperforms specialized state-of-the-art methods on all tasks, with flexible multi-condition control in generation and high-fidelity preservation in editing and completion. SeMo3D further supports agentic and interactive 3D modeling through natural-language interaction.

Our contributions are summarized as follows:

  • •

    We formulate selective modeling, a unified paradigm that casts 3D generation, editing, and completion as synthesizing the designated region while preserving the rest, and present SeMo3D to instantiate this paradigm.

  • •

    We introduce region-selective denoising, which learns all three tasks from standard 3D datasets alone, without costly large-scale paired editing or completion datasets.

  • •

    We develop Omni3DiT, a multi-condition 3D diffusion transformer integrating clean 3D context with image, text, and point guidance for unified controllable 3D creation.

    • 2 Related Work

    3D Generation. Driven by 2D generative models [23, 62, 61, 41, 54, 50], 3D generation has undergone rapid paradigm shifts. Early methods [51, 59, 68, 8, 52] use score distillation sampling (SDS) to lift 2D priors to 3D, but suffer from long optimization times. Multi-view 2D methods [42, 43, 73, 67, 79] accelerate generation by first synthesizing multi-view images and then producing 3D shapes in a feed-forward manner. More recently, native 3D generative models [94, 95, 78, 77, 97, 28, 87, 74, 20, 32] operating directly on 3D latents have pushed quality and scalability further. Despite this progress, most methods condition on a single modality (image or text), limiting fine-grained controllability. Recent efforts incorporate pairwise combinations such as image-text [7, 9] or image-point [75, 29], but none of the above jointly leverages all three modalities to combine the visual detail of images, the semantic expressiveness of text, and the geometric precision of points.

    3D Editing and Completion. 3D editing and completion have evolved analogously: from SDS-based optimization [57, 101, 38, 10, 100, 30, 27] through multi-view 2D methods [4, 35, 3, 18, 16, 70] to native 3D approaches [76, 72, 25, 45, 56, 11]. Native 3D methods are training-free or training-based. Training-free methods [34, 91, 99, 26, 31, 82] repurpose pretrained generators via inversion or optimization; they largely maintain source consistency but require slow, multi-step pipelines. Training-based methods [76, 46, 72, 6, 80, 19, 93, 71, 45, 11, 56, 15, 25] enable fast feed-forward inference but rely on large paired editing or completion datasets (e.g., 100K pairs in PartFlow [72], 116K in 3DEditFormer [76]) and often alter regions that should remain unchanged. Moreover, both lines mostly use a single modality, limiting controllability.

    Unified 3D Multimodal Models. Recent works [90, 88, 85, 86, 89] consolidate multimodal output capabilities into one model, typically unifying 3D understanding with generation and editing [90, 88, 85, 89] or bridging 2D and 3D generation [86]. However, these models are largely built on VLM-based architectures, limiting their native 3D modeling capacity, and their notion of “unity” centers on merging different output modalities (e.g., text, image, and 3D) rather than different 3D creation sub-tasks (generation, editing, and completion). They also typically condition on only one or two modalities, and those that support editing still rely on large-scale paired editing supervision.

    Compared with all three lines of work above, SeMo3D offers a distinct solution: it recasts 3D generation, editing, and completion as a single selective-modeling problem formulated directly on native 3D representations, unifying the three tasks without task-specific architectures or per-task paired supervision while preserving the remaining content by construction. Additionally, SeMo3D supports joint image, text, and point conditioning, enhancing controllability.

    3.1 Preliminaries

    Structured Latents. Following Trellis2 [77], we represent 3D assets as spatially structured latent tokens through a three-stage encoding. The first stage, sparse structure (SS), encodes a 3D asset into a dense latent grid Zˢˢ∈ℝ^N³×dₛ covering all N³ voxels, from which an SS decoder recovers the occupied voxel set O. The second and third stages, collectively termed structured latent (SLat) stages, produce sparse tokens only at positions in O: shape tokens Zˢʰᵃᵖᵉ∈ℝ^|O|×d_g encoding fine geometry, and texture tokens Zᵗᵉˣ∈ℝ^|O|×dₜ encoding PBR materials conditioned on Zˢʰᵃᵖᵉ. Each token at every stage corresponds to a localized spatial region, making the representation amenable to spatially selective operations.

    Rectified Flow Matching. Each stage employs a rectified flow model [41, 39] to generate its respective latent tokens. Given data x₀ and noise ε ∼ ℕ(0,I), the forward process linearly interpolates between them as xₜ=(1-t) x₀+t ε for t ∈ [0,1]. A velocity network v_θ is trained by minimizing the conditional flow matching (CFM) objective:

    L_CFM=𝔼_t, x₀, ε\lVertv_θ(xₜ,t,c)-(ε-x₀)\rVert₂²,

    		(1)

    where c denotes the input conditions, and samples are drawn by integrating the learned ODE from t=1 (pure noise) to t=0 (data). All three stages share this formulation; they differ only in x₀ (Zˢˢ, Zˢʰᵃᵖᵉ, or Zᵗᵉˣ, respectively) and in the model that operates on each.

    Fig.3 illustrates the overall framework. Even without additional point guidance, SeMo3D outperforms all compared methods across all three completion metrics. Unlike point-guided HY3D-Omni, which regenerates whole shapes, SeMo3D preserves existing geometry, synthesizing only the missing part, despite its irregular, non-box shape. In Fig.7, completed regions blend seamlessly with the existing structure. No paired completion data is used; SeMo3D derives this capability purely from region-selective denoising on standard 3D assets, demonstrating the generality of selective modeling.

    4.3 Ablation Study
